title: Token Jumping in Planar Graphs has Linear Sized Kernels

predicted_errors.error_location: Paragraph after Claim 5 ("Since G[J_s ∪ J_t ∪ J_m] is a linear forest, by Claim 4 ...") and end of proof of Claim 7 ("by Claim 4 we move all tokens on ∪{z_i',z_i''} to J_m")
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Both invocations attribute the reconfigurability of token sets inside a linear forest to Claim 4. Claim 4 is the counting statement "If G_{P_Big} has no independent set of size k, then |V(G)| ≤ 40k"; it says nothing about moving tokens. The statement actually needed is Claim 5 ("In every linear forest, every independent set of size k can be reconfigured to every other"). The proof therefore cites the wrong result in the two places where the crucial reconfiguration step is justified.

predicted_errors.error_location: Proof of Claim 7, second branch ("Recall, for each i, that N^Int(Y_i) contains non-adjacent vertices that lie in J_m; call such a pair z_i' and z_i''")
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Nothing earlier guarantees that J_m contains two non-adjacent vertices of each N^Int(Y_i). J_m is merely *some* independent set of size k in G_{P_Big}; it need not meet any particular class N^Int(Y_i) at all, let alone in two vertices. The vertices that are guaranteed to exist and be retained are those added to J_s ("add to J_s the leftmost and right vertex in C_Y as well as two vertices in N^Int(Y), ... giving preference to a non-adjacent pair"). The word "Recall" is thus false, and the set should be J_s, not J_m.

predicted_errors.error_location: Proof of Claim 7, induction over Y_1,...,Y_a
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The stated induction ("For the base case, we move the token on y_1'' to z_1'" and, for i ≥ 2, "move a token from y_i' to z_{i-1}'' and then ... from y_i'' to z_i'") never moves the token sitting on y_1'. Hence the conclusion "Once all tokens are removed from ∪_{i=1}^a Y_i" is not established. Moreover, the base-case move is illegal while y_1' is still occupied, since z_1' ∈ N^Int(Y_1) is adjacent to y_1'. The argument tacitly assumes a prefix of σ emptying y_1' has been replayed, but this is never stated or verified.

predicted_errors.error_location: Paragraph beginning "Henceforth, we assume that G_{P_Big} contains an independent set of size k" and the sentence "Since G[J_s ∪ J_t ∪ J_m] is a linear forest"
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The claim that J_s and J_t each induce a linear forest, and that G[J_s ∪ J_t ∪ J_m] is a linear forest, is unsupported. Claim 3 only guarantees non-adjacency between *interior* vertices of distinct classes (z_i ∈ N^Int(Y_i)). But J_s and J_t explicitly contain the leftmost and rightmost vertices z^ℓ, z^r of each C_Y, which are not interior and may be adjacent to vertices of other classes; such edges can create vertices of degree ≥ 3 or cycles, destroying the linear-forest structure on which the final application of Claim 5 depends.

predicted_errors.error_location: Last line of the proof of Claim 4: "|V(G)| = |X| + |C_1| + |C_2| + |C_3| ≤ 2k + 4k + 26k + 8k = 40k"
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: By the definition C_Y := {v ∈ V(G) : N(v) ∩ X = Y}, every vertex of G—including the vertices of X themselves—lies in exactly one projection class, so V(G) = C_1 ∪ C_2 ∪ C_3 and the displayed identity is not an equality: |X| is counted twice. (The resulting number is still a valid upper bound, but the equation as written is false.)

G' is obtained by deleting only (∪_{Y∈P_Big} N^Int(Y)) \ (J_m ∪ J_s ∪ J_t), so every vertex of C_2 outside ∪_{Y∈P_Big} N^Int(Y) (in particular the leftmost/rightmost vertices z^ℓ, z^r of every class and all of C_Y for Y ∉ P_Big) survives in G'. These are only covered by the term |J_s ∪ J_t ∪ J_m| when the construction of J_s (resp. J_t) does *not* stop early; the construction explicitly allows stopping "up to the point ... where J_s contains an independent set of size k". In that case up to Θ(|P|) retained C_2 vertices are omitted from the count, so the specific bound 67k is not justified (the O(k) conclusion survives).

predicted_errors.error_location: Abstract and Introduction ("fixed-parameter tractable. That is, when k is fixed, the problem can be solved in time polynomial in the order of G.")
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The gloss given for fixed-parameter tractability is the definition of XP (slice-wise polynomial), not FPT. FPT requires running time f(k)·poly(n) with the polynomial degree independent of k, which is strictly stronger. The mis-definition is repeated twice and misrepresents the cited result of Ito, Kamiński, and Ono.

predicted_errors.error_location: Paragraph defining the left-to-right order ("since |f_0| ≥ 3 and y'y'' ∉ E(H_Y), in fact f_0 contains exactly two vertices in C_Y")
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The assertion fails in the degenerate case |C_Y| = 1: then H_Y is the path y'–z–y'', whose outer face contains exactly one vertex of C_Y. Consequently the subsequent definitions (z^ℓ ≠ z^r, N^Int(Y) := C_Y \ {z^ℓ, z^r}) are not well defined for singleton classes, and the recursion's termination case is not addressed.

predicted_errors.error_location: Proof of Claim 3 ("Let C_i := y_i' z_i^ℓ y_i'' z_i^r for each i ∈ {1,2}")
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The symbols C_1 and C_2 were already defined earlier as the unions of projection classes (C_1 := ∪_{|Y|≤1} C_Y, C_2 := ∪_{|Y|=2} C_Y) and are used with that meaning throughout the counting arguments (e.g., "|C_1| < 4k", "|C_2| ≤ 26k"). Reusing C_1 and C_2 for the two four-cycles in Claim 3 makes the statements "z_1 lies inside C_1" ambiguous and conflicts with the established notation.
